title: Machine slide two-speed hydraulic motion requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Preferred fixed-pump open-circuit topology for one horizontal resistive machine-slide cylinder. Tank suction feeds a fixed-displacement pump; pump pressure branches directly to the relief valve and the 4/3 tandem-center DCV. The relief valve and DCV return directly to tank. The DCV A port connects directly to the cylinder cap end. The cylinder rod-end work line passes through exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control, oriented so extension rod-end exhaust flows A-to-B through the throttle to DCV B, while retraction supply from DCV B returns B-to-A through the integral free-reverse path. The same throttled path remains in circuit for rapid approach and working feed; the speed reduction is produced by the load/contact increase rather than by a switched bypass or sequence valve. The tandem neutral unloads the fixed pump to tank while blocking the work ports.

selected_components.name: Tank
selected_components.role: Open-circuit reservoir for pump suction and all hydraulic returns.
configuration: Use S as pump suction source and R as common return sink.

selected_components.name: Pump
selected_components.role: Primary hydraulic supply for the slide circuit.
configuration: Fixed-displacement open-circuit supply; drive and displacement deferred to sizing.
selected_components.selection_basis: No energy-efficiency requirement is stated; fixed pump is the simplest suitable supply.

selected_components.name: Relief Valve
configuration: Connect directly from pump pressure to tank return.
Specify/set as the 20 bar maximum system pressure limiter in sizing.
selected_components.selection_basis: Safety essential requires system pressure not exceed 20 bar.

selected_components.name: 4/3 Solenoid DCV, Tandem Center
selected_components.role: Command extend, neutral, and retract states for the slide cylinder.
configuration: Use extend state P-A and B-T for rapid approach and working feed.
Use retract state P-B and A-T for full return.
Use tandem neutral P-T with A and B blocked to unload the fixed pump when no motion is commanded.
selected_components.selection_basis: Provides bidirectional cylinder control and a fixed-pump neutral unloading path without adding load-control components.

selected_components.name: Double-Acting Cylinder
configuration: Cap end is the extension/toward-workpiece chamber.
Rod end is the retract/return chamber and extension exhaust chamber.
Bore, rod and stroke are deferred to sizing.
selected_components.selection_basis: Single powered extension and powered retraction actuator required by the machine-slide function.

selected_components.name: One-Way Speed Control
selected_components.role: Single load-sensitive non-compensated rod-end meter-out control for extension; free reverse path for retraction supply.
configuration: Install in the rod-end work line between Cylinder.Rod and DCV.B.
Orient A-B as the throttled direction from Cylinder.Rod exhaust toward DCV.B during extension.
Orient B-A as the integral free-reverse check direction from DCV.B toward Cylinder.Rod during retraction.
This is the only speed-control valve for both load-sensitive extension phases.
selected_components.selection_basis: Directive requires exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the declared rod-chamber exhaust meter-out path.

connections.notes: Open-circuit reservoir supplies the fixed-displacement pump inlet.
Pump pressure branches directly to the relief valve inlet for overpressure protection; no isolating device is inserted.
Pump pressure also supplies the directional valve pressure port as the control branch.
Relief discharge returns directly to the reservoir return port.
Directional valve tank port and neutral unloading flow return directly to the reservoir.
DCV A work port supplies the cap end for extension and receives cap-end exhaust during retraction.
Rod-end exhaust during extension enters the A port of the one-way flow control for metered A-to-B flow.
Metered extension exhaust leaves the flow control at B and returns through DCV B-to-T; retraction supply from DCV B uses the valve's internal free-reverse B-to-A path.

motion_control_decisions.justification: This is the faster approach phase of the same extension motion, followed by a specified load-triggered slower feed; load is stated as resisting, with no holding or overrunning requirement.

The slower speed is explicitly required to result from the load increase/contact without an electrical pressure switch; for a horizontal resistive extension requiring deliberate throttled feed, meter-out on rod exhaust is the conventional inferred default.
Return speed is not specified; only return travel and resisting load are stated, with no holding or overrunning requirement.

component_states.reason: Extend command connects P-to-A and B-to-T so the cap end is supplied and rod-end exhaust is forced through the selected rod-end meter-out flow control.

phase_configurations.notes: The one-way flow control has fixed A-to-B metered and B-to-A free-reverse paths; no phase state is required. No unmetered bypass is present.

component_states.reason: Same extend state as rapid approach; the load increase/contact changes pressure drop across the same non-compensated restriction and reduces speed without switching valves.

phase_configurations.notes: The throttle remains in circuit with the same topology and state; no sequence valve, pressure switch, or bypass is used.

component_states.reason: Retract command connects P-to-B and A-to-T, supplying the rod end through the one-way flow control free-reverse path and exhausting the cap end directly to tank.

phase_configurations.notes: Return speed is sizing-only; no separate return speed-control component is selected.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S and the fixed-displacement Pump.P provides open-circuit pressure flow to the relief branch and DCV supply branch. Drive hardware and displacement remain sizing tasks.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with 20 bar relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReliefValve.P is connected directly to Pump.P and ReliefValve.T returns directly to Tank.R. The valve is specified in sizing as the 20 bar maximum-pressure limiter.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Double-acting slide cylinder with 4-way directional control
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV extend state powers SlideCylinder.Cap and exhausts SlideCylinder.Rod through the B-to-T path; DCV retract state powers the rod end through port B and exhausts the cap end through A-to-T.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Single non-compensated rod-end meter-out control for load-caused two-speed extension
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: SlideCylinder.Rod connects to RodEndMeterOutFlowControl.A and RodEndMeterOutFlowControl.B connects to DCV.B. During both extension phases, rod exhaust is throttled A-to-B before reaching DCV B-to-T. The higher work load reduces pressure drop across the non-compensated restriction, reducing extension speed. During retraction, DCV supplies B and the same component permits free reverse B-to-A flow into the rod chamber.
Only one actuator is selected for the slide function, so no flow divider, hydraulic series circuit, or synchronization valve is required.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement open-circuit pump supply.
design_decisions.rationale: No energy-efficiency or standby-unloading requirement is stated, and the selected tandem-center DCV unloads the fixed pump in neutral.
driven_by: Selected a fixed-displacement pump because no energy-efficiency or standby-unloading requirement is stated and the brief allows fixed pump preference.
Open-circuit reservoir supplies pump suction and accepts returns.

design_decisions.decision: Use a direct relief valve from pump pressure to tank for the 20 bar maximum-pressure limit.
design_decisions.rationale: The relief valve is connected directly to the pump pressure branch and returns to tank, providing the required overpressure protection when set/specified to 20 bar in sizing.
driven_by: Selected a simple relief valve from pump pressure to tank as the system overpressure protection device; its 20 bar setting is a sizing/specification task.
Safety essential requires maximum system pressure protection at 20 bar.

design_decisions.decision: Use a 4/3 tandem-center DCV for extend, neutral unloading, and retract.
design_decisions.rationale: The 4-way DCV provides P-to-A/B-to-T extension and P-to-B/A-to-T retraction. Tandem neutral unloads the fixed pump to tank while blocking work ports, with no separate load-holding valve because the slide is treated as horizontal/resistive and no holding or hose-burst retention requirement is stated.
driven_by: Selected a 4/3 tandem-center DCV so the fixed pump is unloaded in neutral while the work ports are blocked; no separate load-holding valve is added because the slide is horizontal/resistive and no holding or hose-burst retention requirement is stated.
Single horizontal slide must advance, work, and return.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-end meter-out path.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected topology forces rod-end exhaust during extension through the A-to-B throttled path and permits retraction supply through the B-to-A free-reverse path. The same non-compensated restriction stays active for both rapid approach and working feed, so speed decreases as load/contact increases without an electrical pressure switch or switched hydraulic bypass.
driven_by: Placed exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-end line, oriented so cylinder rod exhaust during extension is throttled and reverse flow into the rod end during retraction is free.
The same A-B throttled path meters rod-end exhaust during both extension phases; the higher work load reduces pressure drop and therefore flow through the non-compensated restriction.
During retraction, DCV supplies B and flow passes through the flow control B-A free-reverse path to the rod chamber.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add a sequence valve, pressure switch, position valve, second pump, unloading valve, external bypass check, or synchronization device.
design_decisions.rationale: The required rapid-to-feed behavior is achieved by load-sensitive throttling through one selected flow-control component. Additional switched or bypass hardware would defeat or alter the selected mechanism and is not requested; only one actuator is present, so synchronization is not required.
driven_by: Did not add a sequence valve, pressure switch, position valve, second pump, unloading valve, or external bypass check because the speed change is required to result from the load/contact change through the fixed restriction.
Only one actuator is selected; no divider or synchronization valve is included.

assumptions: The slide load is horizontal/resistive as stated by the selected plan; no overrunning, suspended, gravity-lowering, hose-burst retention, or timed no-drift holding requirement is imposed.
The relief-valve 20 bar setting, cylinder dimensions, pump displacement/flow, and flow-control setting are sizing tasks rather than topology changes.
Solenoid actuation is a property of the selected DCV class; no electrical interface is represented in the hydraulic topology.
open_issues: Sizing must verify cylinder area, pump flow, restriction setting, pressure drops, and relief setting tolerance so both approximate speeds and the 20 bar limit are met.
Return initiation logic and return speed are unspecified and are outside this topology selection.
Acceptance tolerances for the approximate rapid and feed speeds are not specified.

research_coverage.summary: The basic open-circuit power/relief topology and the double-acting cylinder with 4-way directional control are adequately supported. Meter-out speed control at the cylinder exhaust side, one-way/free reverse flow, and position/cam-based rapid/slow speed sequencing are also supported. However, the critical requirement that the rapid-to-feed transition occur automatically from load/pressure rise at workpiece contact, without an electrical pressure switch, is not yet supported by a real topology source. Existing evidence only shows general load-sensitive flow reduction through a non-pressure-compensated restriction and a separate cam-operated position-transition circuit; it does not establish an automatic pressure/load-actuated fast/slow switching circuit or its connection logic.

items.rationale: Findings include supported component classes and connection placement: reservoir/tank to pump suction, pump outlet pressure line to directional branch, relief valve in parallel/bypass from pump pressure line directly to tank with no shutoff between pump and relief, and return flow to reservoir. Citations include HK Hydraulik, LibreTexts, and a technical thesis/source, with verified excerpts for relief-valve protection and open-circuit return path.

Findings support a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way directional valve, with clear A-to-cap/B-to-rod connections, P-to-A/B-to-T for extension, P-to-B/A-to-T for retraction, and neutral-center behavior guidance including tandem-center pump unloading and cylinder locking. Citations include Power & Motion Tech and other hydraulic technical/training sources.

The evidence supports meter-out speed control, one-way flow-control/check-valve free reverse flow, rod-end exhaust throttling during extension by connection logic, and a cam-operated 2-way bypass for position-based rapid/slow sequencing. It also supports that a non-pressure-compensated restriction is load/pressure-drop sensitive. What remains weak is the required automatic phase transition specifically caused by load rise at workpiece contact: the current sources do not show a load/pressure-actuated valve arrangement that switches/bypasses/restricts the metered path for rapid approach versus working feed.

This critical need is not covered. The follow-up findings explicitly state that no supplied document directly describes an automatic fast/slow or low/high-pressure switching topology. Existing evidence about non-pressure-compensated restrictions only shows continuous load-dependent speed variation, not a supported hydraulic switching topology that changes from rapid approach to slow feed when load/pressure rises, without an electrical pressure switch.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing exact supported claim: a hydraulic pressure/load-actuated fast-to-slow feed circuit can automatically switch at workpiece contact without an electrical pressure switch.

Missing connection logic for that claim: which valve class performs the switch, where it is connected relative to the pump, directional valve, cylinder ports, meter-out restriction, bypass, and tank, and how rising load/pressure closes/opens the rapid bypass or otherwise forces slow-feed flow.
Weak current substitute: non-pressure-compensated meter-out throttling is load-sensitive, but the evidence does not show it can provide a defined two-speed rapid/feed transition topology by itself.

This is not blocking because the open-circuit power/relief, 4-way double-acting cylinder control, and non-compensated rod-end meter-out sub-patterns are supported and correctly composed.

design_review.summary: Valid topology. The circuit provides open-circuit tank-pump supply, direct pump-to-tank relief protection, correct extend and retract directional paths, one double-acting slide actuator, and exactly one non-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-end exhaust meter-out path. The same throttle remains active during both load-sensitive extension phases with no electrical pressure switch, sequence valve, second pump, unloading valve, or external bypass check. Retraction is powered through the integral free-reverse path, and no unsupported holding, hose-burst, synchronization, or load-control requirement is imposed.
